newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Taiwan's man in HK hopeful of better ties.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's man in HK hopeful of better ties.

text.p: Taiwan's representative in Hong Kong said on Saturday Hong Kong's the appointment of shipping magnate Tung Chee-hwa as the territory's leader-designate could help improve Hong Kong-Taiwanese relations.

"He understands Taiwan's situation and the importance of Hong Kong-Taiwanese relations," Cheng An-kuo, general manager of Taiwan's representative office in the British colony, Chung Hwa Travel Agency, told reporters.
"His appointment as (Hong Kong's) chief executive should have a positive effect on the improvement of Hong Kong-Taiwanese relations," he added.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule next July 1 to become a Chinese Special Administrative Region governed by a chief executive elected by a Beijing-controlled commission.
China regards Taiwan as a renegade province and wants to reunite it with the Chinese mainland.
